title: Soybeans and the Des Moines Insert

text.brief: On September 30, 2018, Ambassador Terry Branstad wrote in the Des Moines Register that a leading newspaper on the mainland had refused to print his essay.
text.record: A week earlier China Daily had paid for a four-page supplement in the Register that warned Iowa farmers about the costs of the trade war. The Party's retaliatory tariffs that July had hit soybeans and other farm goods, and analysts found them aimed at counties that had voted for the President in 2016. Soybean exports to the mainland fell from about $12 billion in 2017 to about $3 billion in 2018. The Agriculture Department announced about $28 billion in aid for farmers over two years.
text.reading: The Party picked targets for their weight in American politics rather than their weight in trade, which is Stratagem 26, and then spoke to the farmers in their own paper. Washington answered with aid, and the buyers moved to Brazil.
text.gapText: Business Architecture. American farm exports depended on one buyer that could shift its purchases overnight, and no plan spread that risk before the tariffs came.
text.fix: Build export markets for farm goods in several countries before a trade fight begins, so one buyer cannot hold a state's farmers hostage.
